applicabilityBasis.summary: Freedom Dollar is expressly marketed for merchant payments, sending, and saving at a dollar target. Its white paper describes redemption as swapping to ZANO or supported assets and identifies no legal obligor redeeming for fixed monetary value. Payment use is established; the statutory issuer and monetary-value redemption elements remain unresolved.

references.label: GENIUS Act statutory text: payment stablecoin definition

genius.notes: The project dashboard publishes ZANO reserves and circulating/minted token figures, but is self-reported. The white paper markets payment use and describes redemption as swaps into ZANO or supported assets; no legal issuer or fixed monetary-value redemption obligor is identified. Its no-company claim is not treated as a legal issuerless exemption. No fixed fiat-redemption policy was established. GENIUS remains pre-effective in the reopened implementation materials. No enforcement clearance or independent monthly attestation conclusion is asserted.

references.label: Treasury GENIUS issuance, offer, and sale proposal

sourcesChecked: 2026-10-07 cutoff exact Freedom Dollar authorization queries on OCC, Federal Register, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA, NYDFS and Treasury domains; returned general rulemaking rather than a token-specific authorization.
negativeEvidenceReview.summary: The reopened OCC pending digital-asset bank application table and NYDFS entity directory contain no Freedom Dollar entry. The Federal Register exact Freedom Dollar query through 2026-10-07 returned zero documents. The token white paper and website show no GENIUS approval, application or licensing-intent statement and identify no legal issuer. No qualifying token-specific public authorization was located in this bounded review; confidential, unindexed or differently named filings are not excluded.

references.label: Federal Register exact Freedom Dollar search through review date
